prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1484; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a side impact at an intersection, with the insured's vehicle struck on the driver's side by a second vehicle that entered on a red signal. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy declarations and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the underwriting file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the driver's seat and notes the other vehicle's failure to yield. Responding officers and a bystander confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene.

Entry 4: Reviewed the scene photographs, which confirm the point of impact and the general position of both vehicles. No independent witnesses have been identified beyond the officers and the bystander who gave a brief statement at the scene.

Entry 5: Inspected the insured vehicle and found door panel crush and intrusion along the driver's side, consistent with the described impact. No prior damage to the vehicle has been identified in our records or in the repair history provided.

Entry 6: Claimant reports neck pain beginning the day of the collision, described as a strain that limits rotation. Medical records from the initial visit document the complaint and the findings are consistent with the force and direction of the crash. No prior injury to the neck or upper back has been identified in the medical history.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the treatment plan. The claimant's account of the collision has been the same in every conversation, including the recorded statement, the initial interview, and the written submission.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment records, which show a usual course of physical therapy and follow-up visits. Symptoms have improved steadily and the frequency of visits has tapered as the claimant's range of motion recovered.

Entry 9: Evaluated the injury against the mechanism of loss. The reported neck strain fits the kind and force of a side impact of this type, and the medical reviewer agreed the treatment is reasonable for the diagnosis.

Entry 10: Current status is that the claim remains open pending the final treatment summary and the attorney's demand package. No further coverage questions are outstanding, and the file is being prepared for evaluation of the bodily injury component.
